title: Brake Vacuum Sensor
introduction:
The brake booster reduces the effort needed at the pedal; this procedure concerns its vacuum sensor and electrical connector. I use the illustration as a landmark map: the reservoir is at the left, rigid lines cross above, and the highlighted connector and sensor sit below them.

Give this small part a careful look before moving it. Its exact fitted position is the reassembly reference—this is a small job with a very particular parking spot. The instructions cover removal and refitting, with no diagnostic test or separate access-disassembly sequence.

items.name: Read the applicable precautions
items.detail: Before starting, review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and its applicable referral to [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183). This sensor procedure does not direct hydraulic-fluid handling or work on friction components.

items.name: Disable remote start
items.detail: Before working around the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started during service, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Ignition and key
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an unexpected start can cause serious personal injury. Keep the ignition off when servicing near rotating engine parts. If equipped with auto start-stop, the engine can start automatically with the ignition on, creating a risk of serious personal injury.

items.name: Eye, ear and hand protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to use the required protection can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Check cooling-fan condition
items.detail: With the ignition OFF, inspect all cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation. Do not work under the hood with a damaged fan; replace it with a new fan as necessary. A damaged fan can separate during operation and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Work near cooling fans
items.detail: Cooling fans can run with the ignition off. Disable them before working nearby; unexpected operation can cause personal injury. The sensor instructions do not specify a fan-disabling method.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps for installation details as well.
edits.why: Note the sensor's fitted position before disturbing it so you have the required reference for reassembly.

edits.text: Disconnect the brake booster vacuum sensor electrical connector, then remove the brake booster vacuum sensor.
edits.why: The magenta connector and blue sensor identify the two components involved. I separate disconnecting the wiring from removing the sensor and note the fitted position before disturbing it; the installation instruction requires that exact position again.

edits.text: NOTE: The installation position is critical. Reinstall the sensor in exactly the position it occupied before removal.
edits.why: Compare the refitted sensor with the position noted before removal; the illustration is a location guide, while the original fitted position is the required reassembly reference.

edits.text: Reverse the removal procedure: reinstall the brake booster vacuum sensor in its original position, then reconnect its electrical connector.
edits.why: Completion here means restoring the specified sensor position and electrical connection. These steps do not establish whether a brake-assistance complaint has been diagnosed or resolved.

directionClarification.sourceText: Disconnect the brake booster vacuum sensor electrical connector and remove the brake booster vacuum sensor.

before.text: Release and disconnect the brake booster vacuum sensor electrical connector at the latch shown in the illustration, then remove the brake booster vacuum sensor in the indicated direction.
before.why: The upper arrow identifies the connector release area; the arrow on the blue sensor indicates its withdrawal direction. I use those arrows to distinguish releasing the connector from removing the sensor, rather than treating the highlighted assembly as a single piece.

after.text: Disconnect the brake booster vacuum sensor electrical connector, then remove the brake booster vacuum sensor.
after.why: The magenta connector and blue sensor identify the two components involved. I separate disconnecting the wiring from removing the sensor and note the fitted position before disturbing it; the installation instruction requires that exact position again.

directionClarification.reason: Original image marks do not unambiguously establish a withdrawal direction. Removes inferred release/directional mechanics; preserves the exact source action sequence and installation-position requirement.
